questions.problem: For the function $f(x,y),$ calculate $\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}}$ given that $\frac{∂f}{∂x}=2xy{e}^{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find $\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}}$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $\frac{∂f}{∂x}$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{∂f}{∂x}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2xy{e}^{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}) \\  & =2y\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(x{e}^{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}) \\  & =2y\cdot ({e}^{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}+2{x}^{2}{e}^{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}) \\  & =2y(1+2{x}^{2}){e}^{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: For the function $f(x,y),$ calculate $\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x}$ given that $\frac{∂f}{∂x}=2x{y}^{2}{e}^{{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}.$
For the function $f(x,y),$ calculate $\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y}$ given that $\frac{∂f}{∂y}=\frac{{e}^{y}}{x+y}.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find $\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y}$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $\frac{∂f}{∂y}$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{∂f}{∂y}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{{e}^{y}}{x+y}) \\  & ={e}^{y}\cdot (-\frac{1}{(x+y)^{2}}) \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{y}}{(x+y)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: For the function $f(x,y),$ calculate $\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y}$ given that $\frac{∂f}{∂y}=-\frac{2{x}^{2}+y}{{y}^{3}}.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find $\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y}$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $\frac{∂f}{∂y}$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{∂f}{∂y}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-\frac{2{x}^{2}+y}{{y}^{3}}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{{y}^{3}}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(2{x}^{2}+y) \\  & =-\frac{1}{{y}^{3}}(4x) \\  & =-\frac{4x}{{y}^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: For the function $f(x,y),$ calculate $\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}}$ given that $\frac{∂f}{∂x}=2x\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}).$
questions.worked_solution:
To find $\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}}$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $\frac{∂f}{∂x}$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{∂f}{∂x}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})) \\  & =2\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})+2x\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}))\cdot 2x \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})-4{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing Expressions Involving Second-Order Partial Derivatives
questions.worked_solution:
To find ${f}_{xx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}) \\  & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}+\frac{{x}^{2}}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}\end{aligned}
$$

To find ${f}_{yy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${f}_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}) \\  & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{y}^{2}}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xx}(x,y)+{f}_{yy}(x,y) & =\frac{2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}+\frac{{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{3({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}} \\  & =3\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

To find ${f}_{yx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${f}_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+y}) \\  & =(-\frac{1}{({x}^{2}+y)^{2}})\cdot 2x \\  & =-\frac{2x}{({x}^{2}+y)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y)+{f}_{yx}(x,y) & =-\frac{2x}{({x}^{2}+y)^{2}}-\frac{2x}{({x}^{2}+y)^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{4x}{({x}^{2}+y)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xy}(-1,2) & =-\frac{2}{((-1)+2(2))^{2}}=-\frac{2}{9} \\ {g}_{yx}(-1,2) & =-\frac{2}{((-1)+2(2))^{2}}=-\frac{2}{9}\end{aligned}

$$
{g}_{xy}(-1,2)+{g}_{yx}(-1,2)=-\frac{4}{9}.

{g}_{xx}(0,1)\cdot {g}_{yy}(0,1)=4{e}^{-1}\cdot {e}^{-1}=4{e}^{-2}.

canonical_examples.problem: Find $\dfrac {\partial^2 f }{\partial x\partial y}$ given that $\dfrac {\partial f}{\partial y} =  \dfrac {2y} {x + y^2}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To find $\dfrac {\partial^2 f }{\partial x\partial y},$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $\dfrac {\partial f}{\partial y}$ with respect to $x\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{∂f}{∂y}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{2y}{x+{y}^{2}}) \\  & =2y\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}({(x+{y}^{2})}^{-1}) \\  & =-2y(x+{y}^{2})^{-2}\cdot 1 \\  & =-\frac{2y}{{(x+{y}^{2})}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To find $f_{xy}(x,y),$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $f_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)) \\  & =1\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)+y(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\cdot x) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-xy\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}
$$

 

Similarly, to find $f_{yx}(x,y),$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $f_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $x\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)) \\  & =1\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)+x(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\cdot y) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-xy\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y)+{f}_{yx}(x,y) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-xy\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-xy\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy) \\  & =2(\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-xy\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)).\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Evaluate $g_{xyz}(x,y,z)$ at $(1,2,3)$ if $g_x(x,y,z) = 2x y z +  y^3.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we find $g_{xy}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating $g_{x}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xy}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2xyz+{y}^{3}) \\  & =2xz+3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find $g_{xyz}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating $g_{xy}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $z\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xyz}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(2xz+3{y}^{2}) \\  & =2x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xyz}(1,2,3) & =2(1) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
